body.statement: Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\), along each subsequence with \(\ell_{a,n}\to\ell_a\), \[\frac{n}{H_n}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta)\Rightarrow\ell_1L_1-\ell_0L_0,\] where \(L_a=\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}/f_a\) for \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\) and \(L_a\) is the Gaussian vector generated by \(\mathrm{IF}_a\) for \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\). Unequal heavy indices are dominated by the smaller index, equal heavy indices retain both endpoint constants, a heavy arm dominates a finite-variance arm, and two finite-variance arms retain their shared learned-score covariance. The two oracle-preserved heavy-arm endpoint processes are independent because their rare-event endpoint sets are disjoint.
body.justification: The explicit arm partition makes equal, unequal, and mixed regimes coherent without inventing a Hall index for a bounded arm.
body.gap: The oracle QTE paper gives joint endpoint laws but not recombination with a shared flexible propensity likelihood.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain joint QTE inference when treatment and control have different overlap regimes.
